# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 70 (Bu-Vb Pc70)

**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 70
**Title (English, from literature):** Supporting a novice monk with a bad view

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 70 is the tenth and concluding training rule of the *Sappāṇavagga* in the Pātimokkha [Vinayamukha 1983]. The rule proscribes associating with, sheltering, eating with, or being served by a novice (*sāmaṇera*) who has been expelled from the community for clinging to the false view that things declared obstructive (*antarāyika*) by the Buddha are not genuinely obstructive [SuttaCentral; Wijayaratna 1990; Vinayamukha 1983]. According to the origin narrative, the novice Kaṇḍaka maintained this distorted teaching and refused to relinquish it after being admonished three times [Wijayaratna 1990; Vinayamukha 1983]. Consequently, the Sangha enacted expulsion (*nāsanā* or *nissāranā*) by a formal act of authorization (*apalokanakamma*), barring him from calling the Buddha his teacher and expelling him from the residence; should the expelled novice later acknowledge the fault, he can be reinstated (*osāretabbo*) via another *apalokanakamma* [Wijayaratna 1990; Vinayamukha 1983; Hüsken 1997].
SuttaCentral notes that this rule has direct equivalents across all surviving Vinaya traditions, including the Bhikkhu Pātimokkhas and Vibhaṅgas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, and Mahāsaṅghika traditions (variously enumerated as Pc 47, Pc 50, Pc 57, or Pc 70), as well as corresponding rules for nuns (such as Pali Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 148) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus highlights significant Pali-internal text reuse with the *Alagaddūpama Sutta* (MN 22) and Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 68—both of which detail the identical obstinate view held by the monk Ariṭṭha—as well as the *Kammakkhandhaka* (Kd 11) and *Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta* (MN 38) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus identifies machine alignments with Sanskrit Prātimokṣasūtra manuscripts and Tibetan translations of the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* and Guṇaprabha's *Vinayasūtra* traditions [DharmaNexus].
